points.heading: First conjugation (-ar / cantar)
points.body:
A Spanish verb names an action. To **conjugate** means to change it for the person who acts. An **infinitive** is the dictionary form, such as **cantar**. The **stem** remains after you drop **-ar**; the **ending** is what you add.

**Cantar** belongs to the **-ar** family. With stem **cant-**: yo **canto**, tú **cantas**, él **canta**. **Hablar** follows the same pattern: hablo, hablas, habla.

Practice: Now it's your turn. Your turn. Write yo / tú / él for cantar and hablar. Say them out loud.

Common mistake: Keeping the -ar on the stem (cantaro). Drop -ar first, then add the ending.

points.heading: Second conjugation (-er / comer)
points.body:
**Comer** is an infinitive in the Spanish **-er** family. Its stem is **com-**. Present endings for yo, tú, and él are **-o**, **-es**, and **-e**.

Com- plus -o makes yo **como**; plus -es makes tú **comes**; plus -e makes él **come**. **Beber** works the same way: bebo, bebes, bebe. Notice -er and -ir share -o/-es/-e for these three persons, but the infinitive ending still shows the family.

Practice: Now it's your turn. Your turn. Write yo / tú / él for comer and beber. Circle the endings.

Common mistake: Using -as/-a (from -ar) with comer. Say comes / come, not comas / coma in this present pattern.

points.heading: Third conjugation (-ir / vivir)
points.body:
**Vivir** is an infinitive in the Spanish **-ir** family. Its stem is **viv-**. For yo, tú, and él the present endings are again **-o**, **-es**, and **-e**: **vivo**, **vives**, **vive**.

**Escribir** follows the same route: escribo, escribes, escribe. Compare three infinitives side by side: cantar / comer / vivir. The family label sits on the infinitive; the person shows in the ending.

Practice: Now it's your turn. Your turn. Make a three-column chart for cantar, comer, and vivir (yo, tú, él).

Common mistake: Mixing families: writing «yo vive» or «él canto». Match stem family and person ending.

lesson.summary: Three Spanish verb families: -ar, -er, and -ir. Conjugate cantar, comer, and vivir for yo, tú, and él.
lesson.memoryPhrase: Spanish families: **-ar** (cantar → canto, cantas, canta), **-er** (comer → como, comes, come), **-ir** (vivir → vivo, vives, vive).
